expect: Identify the option-application protocol required to supply two ordinary inputs.
Ordinary arguments or an equally direct construction can remove this protocol at the complete shown uses; demonstrate a call, not a line-count argument.
Do not require a constructor, builder, validation or interface twin.
constraints: Preserve empty strings and prefix/suffix roles; do not invent defaults or absent-value validation.
The usage inventory is explicitly closed and internal; do not generalize this to a released options API.

expect: Retain useful defaults, the valid zero value and the existing options contract without imposing a universal configuration pattern.
Do not conflate omitted/nil labels with explicitly empty labels or introduce cloning as clarity-only cleanup.
constraints: Keep nil/empty, last-option precedence and borrowed slice aliasing.
Released function and option types have consumers beyond the shown calls; no breaking positional rewrite.

expect: Consider slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(m)) as the complete supported operation, with eager collection at the same call.
A standard composition may remove mechanical collection/sort steps; retaining the domain helper is independent of replacing its body.
constraints: Go 1.23 is established, including iterator APIs.
Preserve sorting, eager observation and nil output for no keys; do not return a lazy iterator instead.

expect: Reject the proposed live sequence as an equivalent snapshot cleanup; observation moves after replace.
Keep the existing eager contract or propose only a remedy that retains it; neither iterators nor copies are universally preferred.
constraints: Preserve eager observation, repeated traversal and nil/empty.
A shallow snapshot is sufficient for the shown string elements, not evidence of deep independence for arbitrary types.

expect: io.Copy can express the stated transfer contract without custom buffering and EOF plumbing.
Explain the operation and retained result/error contract; make no allocation or performance claim.
constraints: Read may return data with an error; retain bytes-written results and EOF normalization.
The packet explicitly excludes observable batch-size/optional-interface behavior; absent that evidence the replacement needs qualification.

expect: Keep the explicit record/emit protocol; Copy and ReadAll do not express the whole operation.
Do not replace it with Scanner without establishing delimiter, partial-result and error equivalence.
constraints: Keep record count, delimiters, partial data, original errors and emit-before-read-error ordering.
No missing-error audit, buffering optimization or new record policy.

expect: Identify the boolean-selected lifecycle protocol that requires reconstructing cancel versus completion.
Separate named cancellation and completion handles can express the existing responsibilities without a lifecycle framework.
Do not make start synchronous or move foreground relative to cancellation/join.
constraints: Cancellation is a request, not a join.
Preserve input ownership, output timing, nil/closed input semantics, and who closes done; no race/deadlock/leak audit.

expect: Retain the explicit streaming, cancellation and completion contract without imposing a synchronous or collect-all API.
An applicable lifecycle review can finish without a candidate; do not demand another owner object or an errgroup dependency.
constraints: Do not replace the join with Cancel or move deferred cleanup into a helper returning the subscription.
Keep channel direction, producer close order and foreground return timing.

expect: Identify the tuple of callbacks hiding a single sql.Tx and its owner.
A visible BeginTx/use/Commit with deferred Rollback at saveBatch, retaining a meaningful SQL helper if useful, can remove the callback protocol.
Do not introduce a transaction manager, service locator, DI container or DBTX interface by default.
constraints: Keep begin/write/commit/deferred-rollback timing and exact operation errors, including commit failure.
No altered isolation, retry, empty-input or rollback-error policy; no SQL execution.

expect: Keep the visible owner/participant contract; merely accepting *sql.Tx does not justify an interface or another layer.
Reject moving acquisition and defer into a helper returning tx, or moving operations outside the transaction for a tidier function.
constraints: Preserve effect/defer order, transaction scope and original errors.
Evaluate expression, not missing rollback handling, SQL validity, retries or isolation.

expect: The job caller fabricates HTTP representation only to call an operation that already accepts an email.
Decode the query at the HTTP adapter and use the existing Send contract for both paths, or an equally justified narrow operation.
Do not replace one forwarding layer with a new service/repository/mapper hierarchy.
constraints: Preserve query Get semantics, empty values, context and Send error identity.
Keep HTTP status and output mapping at the adapter; do not invent new validation or capabilities.

expect: Retain the cohesive HTTP adapter and supported ServeContent mechanism.
No service/repository or copied byte result is justified solely because a handler reads and renders.
constraints: Keep deferred close at handler return, seekable content, range/conditional response semantics and status mapping.
No filesystem-security, missing-close, performance or business-logic audit.

expect: Accept the supported implementation-only simplification in the go1.23-constrained file without increasing the module minimum.
Check the !go1.23 fallback and unchanged consumer-visible []string signature; mutually exclusive files do not coexist.
constraints: Keep Go 1.22 consumers and the old implementation.
No iter.Seq in the common public API; preserve eager sorting and nil output.

expect: Withhold the Go 1.23-only replacement in the untagged nested module; the installed/root toolchain is not its consumer baseline.
Retain any supported quality observation without presenting an upgrade as authorized implementation advice.
constraints: Nearest go.mod and supported consumers govern; absence of a fallback is supplied evidence.
Successful compilation on a newer toolchain is not an MSRV check.

expect: maps.Clone expresses the complete stated shallow-copy operation on the supported baseline.
Keep the meaningful snapshot boundary when useful; do not promise deep independence.
constraints: Preserve nil versus writable empty and the shared pointed-to values.
No mutation-policy redesign or immutable framework.

expect: Reject the unqualified whole-body Clone replacement because nil input no longer yields a writable map.
A guarded standard operation may be discussed without demanding it; the current small loop is a valid expression.
constraints: Preserve nil-to-writable-empty behavior and shallow aliases.
The issue is proposed-refactor compatibility, not a nil-map bug in current source.

expect: Reject moving stop to a helper that returns before consumption; preserve early termination at the consuming owner.
Do not pre-count, replay or fully materialize a possibly single-use sequence to simplify this caller.
constraints: Preserve defer scope, at-most-two consumption and nil output when no values exist.
No general missing-stop, leak or performance pass.

expect: Reject replacing allocating selection with an in-place deletion on the input.
Cloning plus deletion needs an explicit nil/empty and aliasing comparison, not an automatic preference over this loop.
constraints: Preserve independent storage, original aliases, ordering and non-nil empty output.
DeleteFunc mutates storage and supported versions clear the removed tail; no allocation or race claim.
